reason: 'How do I freeze my bank card' is the compromised-card action while 'strange withdrawal' is the unrecognised-withdrawal complaint; both labels fit.
'message saying that my transfer is not possible' names no beneficiary, so declined_transfer, failed_transfer and beneficiary_not_allowed are all defensible.
'contact customer support about a transfer' states no problem at all, so no transfer intent (least of all declined_transfer) can be read from the words.
'buy some crypto ... I really want to exchange this' is an in-app exchange request with no transfer or beneficiary anywhere in the text.
'a pound charge ... described as ... Pending' is the unexplained small charge on the statement, but 'never changed during the last two days' also reads as a stuck pending card payment.
'charged for a SEPA transfer' names a rail used both for topping up and for sending money, and the text gives no direction.
'concerned about the security in my account ... make a dispute' mentions no direct debit, card or transaction type.
'charged for something I didn't expect' names no transfer, card payment or fee type.
'new card to replace an old one' suggests a renewal but never says expiry, and 'when I will receive' is a delivery-time question.
'how do i get a card' is an ordering question while 'if i am in the usa' makes country availability the crux.
'locate my card' could mean a card the user has lost or a card still in the post that they want tracked.
'waiting for my transaction to go through' does not say whether it is a transfer, card payment or top-up, nor who the recipient is.
'friends ... top it up for me' says neither card nor bank transfer, so topping_up_by_card and receiving_money are both defensible.
'What happens if a merchant doesn't accept a payment' could be a reverted payment, a declined payment or card acceptance; the text picks none.
'I need to make a transfer, what will the fee be' is an outbound transfer fee question with no mention of topping up.
'paid for my top up twice by accident ... get a refund' is a double charge; nothing was reverted.
'charge me for a SEPA transfer' gives no direction, so a top-up by bank transfer and an outbound transfer fee are both defensible.
'wondering when my card will get here' is both a delivery-time question and a customer waiting on a card in transit.
'transfer to an account was not allowed' fits beneficiary_not_allowed, but 'not allowed' is also how a declined transfer is described.
'Weird charges ... in my debit account' says debit account, not direct debit, and names no transaction type.
'How do I accept exchanges to EU' is garbled but is about exchanging into euros (exchange_via_app or fiat_currency_support), not about where a card is accepted.
'How long will it take for my transferred money to show up' is a generic transfer-timing question, not a report of an incoming bank transfer that has failed to arrive.
'friends able to top up my account' names no method, so topping_up_by_card and receiving_money are both defensible.
'the $1 transaction' is the unexplained small charge on the statement; there is no transfer for transfer_timing.
'will not let me into my account' gives no cause, so forgotten passcode, identity verification and PIN block are all possible.
'put a freeze on my card' is the compromised-card action while 'payments on it and I don't know what for' is the unrecognised-payment complaint.
'theft-top option' is garbled; it may mean 'auto top-up', 'the top-up' or a theft option, and the text cannot settle it.
'charged on my account that shouldn't be there' names no direct debit, card or transfer.
'How long does a card delivery take' is a generic delivery-time estimate, not a customer reporting a card that has not arrived.
'My card was not accepted' could be a declined payment, a card not working or a merchant not accepting the card.
'strange charges on my card that I didn't make' is an unrecognised payment while 'Is my card stolen ... should I cancel it' is a compromised card.
'Are US credit cards accepted' asks whether the bank takes other issuers' cards, not where the bank's own card is accepted.
'transfer money to a beneficiery. Why can't I' names the beneficiary as the blocker.
'I need my card to come as soon as possible' is a customer waiting on a card and asks for speed rather than an estimate; both labels fit.
'How long can I expect a transfer to pend for' is a generic timing question, but 'pend' points at pending_transfer.
'total cost of a transfer' is a transfer fee question; nothing in the text says top-up.
'1 other US card, can you take it' asks whether a foreign card is supported; no top-up is mentioned.
'When I got cash ... overcharged me' could be an unexpected withdrawal fee or a debit larger than the cash received.
'completed an in country transfer ... funds are still not available' does not say whether the user sent or received the money.
'authorise a payment' is a card payment awaiting authorisation; there is no transfer for transfer_timing.
'How do I freeze my card' gives no reason, so compromised_card and lost_or_stolen_card are equally defensible.
'transfer money using my card ... the money disappeared' is a card top-up that has not landed, neither a how-to (topping_up_by_card) nor a bank transfer (failed_transfer).
'your exchange rate is [not] right ... check the official interbank exchange' is a general rate complaint with no card payment mentioned.
'make a currency exchange to EU' is an exchange request (exchange_via_app) but also a question about euro support (fiat_currency_support).
'error message saying that my transfer was not possible' names no beneficiary, so declined_transfer, failed_transfer and beneficiary_not_allowed are all defensible.
'how to top up my account' names no method, so card and bank-transfer top-up are equally defensible.
'random withdrawal in my app' is an unrecognised withdrawal, not a declined one.
'Are both Visa and Mastercard accepted' could ask which network the bank issues or which cards it takes; it is not about merchants accepting the card.
'awaiting the completion of the transaction' names no transaction type or recipient.
'money I pushed ... as being withdrawn' is garbled; it could be a sent transfer or a debited-but-undelivered withdrawal, and never mentions an amount of cash.
'my new card can be renewed' is contradictory; 'renewed' says expiry replacement but 'new card' suggests the user may mean activation.
'What currencies will this app exchange' asks which currencies are supported, not how to exchange.
'How long should my new card take to arrive' is a delivery-time question about a specific card, so both labels fit.
'charged for a withdraw ... that was decline' is both a declined withdrawal and a debit still sitting on the account.
'send the new card to China' asks about delivery to a country (order_physical_card is the other fit) and never mentions expiry.
'When will the card arrive' fits both a delivery estimate and a card-arrival query.
'Ordered awhile back' is a customer waiting on a card while 'what is the ETA' asks for a delivery estimate.
